messages:
alex: Heads-up — I’m seeing a small but consistent Xid0/Xid13 uptick in eu-west after last night’s driver+kernel push. Not full outage, but 2.5x above our 30d baseline on ~6 hosts.

priya: ack. are those the same physical cards we saw flaking two weeks ago?

alex: overlap is partial. I correlated by serial, looks like 3 reused cards and 3 different ones. Query I ran: 
```
-- telemetry quick count
SELECT host, gpu_serial, count(*) as xid_count
FROM gpu.events
WHERE xid_code IN (0,13)
  AND ts >= '2025-10-08T00:00:00Z'
  AND ts < '2025-10-09T08:00:00Z'
GROUP BY host, gpu_serial
ORDER BY xid_count DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

sam: thanks. can you add kernel version + driver version to that result? want to see if it lines up to the rollout wave.

alex: done, added columns. all 6 hosts are on kernel 6.2.14 + driver 515.12.1. Older hosts staying at 6.1 line have none of the uptick.

maya: hmm — could be a kernel-driver interaction at the PCI error handler boundary. we should not do a full rollback yet. propose: build a short synthetic validation job that reproduces the load pattern from the last week and run it on a canary pool (eu-west canary set). If it reproduces, we gate.

priya: +1. keep it tight: 30m warmup, then 2h steady state of mixed batch inference + sustained KV cache pressure. That tends to trigger the stateful bug when present.

deploy-bot: scheduled: synthetic-xid-stress-run on pool=eu-west-canary at 2025-10-09T13:00:00Z by maya. job id: sb-33721

alex: job ran. early results: two GPUs showed Xid13 at 22m and 35m into the steady state, both on same kernel/driver combo. Logs attached to job sb-33721 in S3: s3://redwood-test-logs/sb-33721/

sam: can you paste the GPU dmesg excerpt? particularly the pci channel errors and iommu lines.

alex: pasted below: 
```
Oct 09 13:22:04 host-03 kernel: NVRM: Xid (13, 0x00000000): PID 21501: on GPU 1: Channel 00000000
Oct 09 13:22:04 host-03 kernel: pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=0001
Oct 09 13:22:04 host-03 kernel: iommu: Removing device 0000:03:00.0 from domain
```

maya: that sequence is suspicious — AER correcteds followed by Xid. Could be an upstream PCIe instability that the driver isn't tolerating after this kernel change.

priya: test plan proposal:
- Run synthetic workload on 10 canary hosts (mix old/new cards)
- Add a power-cycle subtest: cold reset the card after 1h of steady state on 2 hosts
- Attach iLO/BMC logs and PCIe AER counters before/after
- Run two driver variants: 515.12.1 (rolled) and 515.11.9 (previous) side-by-side
- Collect `nvidia-smi -q -d BUS` and `dmesg` dumps every 5m

sam: sounds good. also add a kernel patch try: 6.2.14-rc2 with the pci/aer backport we discussed. Might be a micro fix.

alex: I ran a quick cost calc — running the canary stress across 10 hosts x 3h = ~30 GPU-hours. With reserved pricing that’s ~ $360 of incremental infra cost for the test. good trade for not rolling back.

maya: agree. priority is preventing noisy rollback. Also add an alert to mute normal pager for this canary pool (so escalations on known test noise don’t hit oncall).

deploy-bot: alert-mute applied: channel=eng-sre, scope=eu-west-canary, duration=4h, by=maya

priya: one more metric we should gate on: Xid rate normalized by GPU-hours and by PCIe corrected error rate. set gating thresholds: fail if Xid_rate > 0.5 per GPU-hour AND PCIe_AER_incr > 10 events in 1h.

sam: adding regression harness changes to the CI: new smoke job `xid-regression` that runs the synthetic workload against both driver versions and reports a pass/fail. will open PR.

alex: after the run we had 4 total Xids across the 10 hosts, all on 515.12.1 hosts, 0 on 515.11.9. PCIe AER increments were +37 on two failed hosts, +3 on others.

maya: that’s a pretty clear signal. recommendation: pause the rollout on eu-west, mark 515.12.1 as suspect, and escalate to vendor with attached dmesg + PCIe counters. also schedule a replacement probe for the two cards that had persistent resets (serials: GPU-8C2, GPU-9D7).

priya: agree. add short-term mitigation: in the pool routing policy, prefer hosts on kernel 6.1 line for latency-sensitive routes until we have a vendor fix. Update traffic weighting to shift 15% away from eu-west 6.2 hosts.

sam: PR opened for `xid-regression` CI job: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/ci/pulls/482 (adds parallel driver runs and artifact upload).

alex: vendor ticket opened (NV-22147) with attached sb-33721 logs, dmesg, and AER counters. Vendor acknowledged and requested additional `ndev` debug logs — I uploaded them.

maya: good run everyone. next steps:
- pause rollout in eu-west (prod hold) — ops to enforce
- schedule replacement + burnin for suspect cards in next maintenance window
- keep canary loop in place and run with updated kernel variant when vendor suggests patch
- if vendor patch doesn't reduce AER->Xid chain in 48h, prepare rollback plan for driver to 515.11.9

priya: tagging @oncall for awareness (we muted alerts for canary but want human eyes if it leaks).

alex: rolling the pause now. Will post follow-ups when vendor replies or if we see new noisy hosts. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks — closing thread unless new evidence. :rocket:
